Summary of mvgam model fits

Source: R/summary.mvgam.R
summary.mvgam.Rd

Provides posterior summary statistics for mvgam model parameters, organised by category (fixed effects, smooth terms, family parameters, trend parameters and factor loadings).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
summary(object, probs = c(0.025, 0.975), robust = FALSE, matrices = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

object

An object of class mvgam.

probs

Numeric vector of probabilities for quantile computation. Default is c(0.025, 0.975) for 95% credible intervals. Can be a single value or multiple values.

robust

Logical. If FALSE (the default), uses mean and standard deviation for summaries. If TRUE, uses median and median absolute deviation (MAD).

matrices

Logical; if TRUE, also print every cell of the matrices a correlated, VAR or hierarchical trend derives from its sampled parameters (Phi_trend, Sigma_trend, Omega_trend, Phi_group_trend, Sigma_group_trend). The default FALSE prints the sampled parameters alone, among them sigma_trend, Amu_trend, Aomega_trend and alpha_cor_trend. posterior_transition_matrix() and residual_cor() summarise the matrices a cell at a time.

...

Unused. Anything passed here is refused.

Value

An object of class mvgam_summary. Each block is a data frame of the columns below, one row per parameter, named as print() shows it. A block is absent when the model has no such parameter. The observation model's blocks are:

smooth

Smoothing standard deviations, one row per penalty of each smooth. The basis coefficients are available by name from as_draws(object, variable = "^s_", regex = TRUE).

gp

Gaussian-process marginal standard deviations and length-scales.

random

Group-level standard deviations and correlations, as a list of tables named by grouping factor. ngrps gives each factor's number of levels. ranef() gives the per-level effects.

fixed

Regression coefficients, those of every distributional parameter given a formula among them.

mo

The simplex of each monotonic effect.

spec

Family parameters without a formula of their own, such as sigma or shape.

The trend model's blocks take the same names with the prefix trend_, joined by trend_spec for the trend's dynamics, loadings for the factor loadings and loadings_prior for the hyperparameters of their prior. The formula, family, draw counts and data dimensions are stored with them.

Details

Each block has the columns:

Estimate

Posterior mean, or median with robust = TRUE.

Est.Error

Posterior standard deviation, or MAD with robust = TRUE.

l-95% CI, u-95% CI

Credible interval bounds at probs, labelled by its coverage.

Rhat

Potential scale reduction factor on split chains, 1 at convergence.

Bulk_ESS, Tail_ESS

Bulk and tail effective sample sizes.

See also

how_to_cite() drafts a methods paragraph for the model. methods_md() writes its equations, glossary and priors. mcmc_plot.mvgam() plots the draws of these parameters.

Other posterior summaries: VarCorr.mvgam(), bibtex(), how_to_cite.mvgam(), hypothesis.mvgam(), index-mvgam, mcmc_plot.mvgam(), methods_md(), mvgam_draws, pairs.mvgam(), posterior_interval.mvgam(), ranef.mvgam(), smooths.mvgam()

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(13)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                     n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())
mod <- mvgam(y ~ s(x), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
              data = simdat$data_train,
              family = poisson(),
              chains = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 9 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

summary(mod)
#>  Family: poisson 
#>   Links: mu = log 
#> Formula: y ~ s(x) 
#>    Data: simdat$data_train (Number of observations: 90) 
#>  Trends: AR(1) 
#>   Draws: 2 chains, each with iter = 2000; warmup = 1000; thin = 1; 
#>          total post-warmup draws = 2000
#> 
#> == Observation Model ==
#> Smoothing Spline Hyperparameters:
#>           Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Rhat Bulk_ESS Tail_ESS
#> sds(sx_1)     4.32      1.65     1.93     8.28 1.00      583      999
#> 
#> Regression Coefficients:
#>           Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Rhat Bulk_ESS Tail_ESS
#> Intercept     1.63      0.14     1.36     1.92 1.01      791      571
#> sx_1          7.70      4.92    -1.81    17.73 1.00      785     1102
#> 
#> == Trend Model ==
#> Trend Specific Parameters:
#>                       Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Rhat Bulk_ESS
#> sigma_trend[series_1]     0.44      0.07     0.30     0.59 1.00      575
#> ar1_trend[series_1]       0.59      0.15     0.28     0.85 1.01      407
#>                       Tail_ESS
#> sigma_trend[series_1]     1100
#> ar1_trend[series_1]        955
#> 
#> Draws were sampled using sampling(NUTS). For each parameter, Bulk_ESS
#> and Tail_ESS are effective sample size measures, and Rhat is the potential
#> scale reduction factor on split chains (at convergence, Rhat = 1).
#> 
#> Next steps:
#>   - `pp_check(fit)`: posterior predictive checks
#>   - `forecast(fit, newdata = ...)`: out-of-sample forecasts
#>   - `lfo_cv(fit)`: leave-future-out model comparison
#>   - `conditional_effects(fit)`: covariate effects
#> Use `how_to_cite(fit)` for a methods paragraph and `methods_md(fit)` for its equations.

# Each block is a data frame, such as the trend's dynamics
round(summary(mod)$trend_spec, 2)
#>                       Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Rhat Bulk_ESS
#> sigma_trend[series_1]     0.44      0.07     0.30     0.59 1.00   575.18
#> ar1_trend[series_1]       0.59      0.15     0.28     0.85 1.01   407.26
#>                       Tail_ESS
#> sigma_trend[series_1]  1099.50
#> ar1_trend[series_1]     954.86

# Next: how_to_cite() drafts the methods paragraph
# }
